notes:
• Blurred layers inside groups (e.g. soft "Shadow" rectangles with a layer
  blur) stay soft. The group's precomp now leaves room for the blur, so
  After Effects no longer cuts it off into a hard-edged box. Same for drop
  shadows on layers inside groups.
• Fill blend modes come across: a gradient or colour overlay set to Multiply,
  Screen, Overlay etc. on the fill itself now blends with the picture
  underneath, like in Figma (it used to sit on top in Normal mode and wash
  the picture out). Image fills keep their blend mode too.
• Gradients that fade to transparent come in as native, editable After
  Effects layers: a Gradient Ramp for the colours plus a luma track matte
  for the transparency (2-stop linear, or radial from the centre). Others
  still use Figma's exact render.
• Bullet and numbered lists also keep exactly the line breaks Figma shows.
